column4: Visit note | 2025-04-20 04:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Gautam Sen, 40, male. Mr. Sen mentions that he experiences cramping belly pain and that his symptoms feel worse with stress. He is a hotel receptionist and notes that his discomfort flares on long commutes through traffic in Chattogram. He denies any fever, bleeding, or weight loss. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 114/79 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 50 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the lower quadrants and no organomegaly. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 02:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Iffat Karim, 77, female. Mrs. Karim reports no other complaints apart from discovering a high reading on a pharmacy machine. She is a retired civil servant whose reading was found during a free health camp in Tangail. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual disturbances. On examination: BP 172/104 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 74 kg. Heart sounds are normal and chest is clear. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: referral to Endocrinology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up after the Endocrinology review.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 04:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Tuhin Mondal, 58, male. Mr. Mondal describes having a creaking knee, knee pain on the stairs, and stiffness in the morning for a few minutes. He works as an NGO field officer and states his symptoms are worse since moving to a building with no lift in Barishal. He denies any recent injury or joint locking. On examination: BMI 29.3, BP 128/74 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 94 kg. Right knee shows mild crepitus and tenderness along the joint line with normal range of motion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-04-26 10:00 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Farida Akand, 72, female. Mrs. Akand presents with high cholesterol on a routine test, noting she has no symptoms and a father who had a heart attack at 55. She works as a tailor and her high reading was found on a pre-employment test in Rajshahi. She denies chest discomfort, palpitations, or dizziness. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.4 mmol/L, BP 121/82 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 49 kg. Cardiovascular exam is unremarkable. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a fasting lipid profile and liver function tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-04-27 10:30 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Parvez Hasan, 73, male. Mr. Hasan reports symptoms worse in air conditioning along with gritty burning eyes. He is a madrasa teacher and mentions his discomfort is worse since night shifts at a call centre in Rangpur. He has a history of Hypothyroidism. He denies eye discharge, pain, or sudden vision loss. On examination: tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 125/84 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 95 kg. Conjunctiva is clear with mild dryness noted. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-04-27 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tamanna Alam, 35, female. Ms. Alam explains that she has stools that switch between loose and hard along with abdominal bloating. She is a bank officer and notes her symptoms are worse since starting a high-pressure job in Tangail. She denies fever or unintended weight loss. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 117/81 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 47 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild general tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-04-28 10:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Bushra Shikder, 31, female. Ms. Shikder complains of extra hair on the face and irregular periods. She works as a textile engineer and noticed these signs after a friend in Mohammadpur suggested testing. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies headaches or vision changes. On examination: BMI 28.2, BP 116/75 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 81 kg. Mild facial hirsutism is observed. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-05-01 02:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Rozina Molla, 22, female. Ms. Molla reports extra hair on the face, weight gain, and irregular periods. She works as a software developer and noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Jatrabari. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies severe pelvic pain or dizziness. On examination: BMI 30.5, BP 125/73 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 64 kg. Examination confirms mild hirsutism and generalized adiposity. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-05-01 02:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Bikash Sarkar, 26, male. Mr. Sarkar comes in for marks left after pimples, pimples and blackheads on the face, and spots on the back. He works as a textile engineer and states his condition flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Gulshan. He denies systemic symptoms or scarring elsewhere. On examination: about 30 inflamed spots on the face, BP 135/75 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 83 kg. Face and upper back show papules, pustules, and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze spots. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-05-01 04:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nargis Gazi, 32, female. Mrs. Gazi complains of weight gain and irregular periods. She works as a delivery rider and noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Jatrabari. She denies abnormal discharge or severe pain. On examination: BMI 31.4, BP 129/71 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 74 kg. Abdominal examination is soft and non-tender. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-05-03 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Bikash Nath, 74, male. Mr. Nath reports numbness in the toes and mentions symptoms are worse at night. He works as a farmer and notes his discomfort is worse since walking barefoot at home in Dhanmondi. He has a history of Hypothyroidism. He denies muscle weakness or balance problems. On examination: reduced sensation at 7 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 133/71 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 68 kg. Lower limb reflexes are sluggish. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: HbA1c, vitamin B12, and a nerve conduction study; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-05-05 10:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Ibrahim Molla, 19, male. Mr. Molla presents with spots on the back and marks left after pimples, showing deep painful lumps along the jawline only. He works as a garment factory worker and mentions his breakout flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Tangail. He denies fever or joint pain. On examination: about 24 inflamed spots on the face, BP 119/71 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 81 kg. Skin displays cystic lesions along the jaw and papules on the back. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze spots. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-05-05 04:00 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Ziaur Islam, 45, male. Mr. Islam complains of itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees, noting symptoms are worse in winter. He works as an NGO field officer and states the condition started after working with cleaning chemicals in Tongi. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies blistering or widespread scaling. On examination: affected area about 3 cm across, BP 112/77 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 59 kg. Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with dry scaling over extensor surfaces. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-05-06 03:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Nurul Ahmed, 73, male. Mr. Ahmed has no other complaints, though he reports headaches on waking and occasional dizziness. He is a shopkeeper whose blood pressure was picked up at a pharmacy in Khulna while buying other medicines. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual changes. On examination: BP 162/102 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 90 kg. Heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-05-06 03:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Tuhin Sarkar, 44, male. Mr. Sarkar describes having tense muscles, poor sleep, and constant worry for months. He works as an architect and states his symptoms are worse since job insecurity at a company in Rajshahi. He denies panic attacks or suicidal ideation. On examination: GAD-7 score 18, BP 119/85 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 66 kg. Patient appears anxious with tense posture. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.
